ai.description: *Rhacophorus verrucopus* is a medium-sized frog (45–60 mm) with a brown dorsum featuring distinct tubercles. It possesses large, fully webbed feet and a white venter with dark mottling.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Rhacophorus verrucopus* is distinguished by the presence of distinct, prominent glandular warts scattered across its dorsal surface, which are absent in similar congeners.
ai.habitat: *Rhacophorus verrucopus* inhabits subtropical evergreen forests and bamboo thickets in the Eastern Himalayas, typically at elevations between 1,000 and 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: *Rhacophorus verrucopus* is primarily nocturnal, remaining inactive in tree hollows or dense vegetation during the day and emerging at night to forage for small insects.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Rhacophorus verrucopus* breeds during the monsoon, depositing foam nests containing approximately 100–150 eggs on vegetation overhanging water bodies.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Rhacophorus verrucopus* is found in the northeastern Indian state of Arunachal Pradesh, typically inhabiting high-altitude forest regions.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Rhacophorus verrucopus* consists of a series of short, high-pitched, pulsed notes emitted from vegetation near mountain streams.
